newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen says will welcome ASEAN envoys.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen says will welcome ASEAN envoys.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said on Monday he would welcome envoys from ASEAN back to Phnom Penh but did not say what their role would be in helping end the country's political crisis.
"Now we are ready to welcome a new special envoy of ASEAN soon," Hun Sen said when asked to clarify his position on any intervention by the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
In a statement last week, Hun Sen said ASEAN had a role to play in preventing foreign interference.
ASEAN sent three foreign ministers to Phnom Penh earlier this month to try to help negotiate a solution to the turmoil after Hun Sen's ouster of First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Hun Sen flatly rejected their mediation proposal.
Foreign Minister Ung Huot later said ASEAN could play a mediation role, throwing the regional grouping into confusion over what role it might be allowed to play.
ASEAN asked Ung Huot to clarify Cambodia's position.
Ung Huot, on returning to Phnom Penh from ASEAN meetings in Kuala Lumpur on Sunday evening, said Cambodia would welcome an ASEAN team.
"Certainly we welcome ASEAN to come and talk with us on whatever issue will bring political stability to this country," he said.
Cambodia's membership in ASEAN was postponed after Hun Sen's violent ouster of Ranariddh on July 6 and the group still recognises Ranariddh as first prime minister.
Ung Huot, when asked if he expected ASEAN to recognise him as first prime minister after the National Assembly approves the nomination, said he was optimisitic.
"It's up to ASEAN, but I expect this," he told reporters.
